comments.body:
Apologies for the delay on my end. 
 
 
I followed the instructions by downloading and starting up the one click run Fedora, then downloaded and attempted to run the import export utility but got the following error:
 
Samuels-Educopia-MacBook-Pro-8:downloads samalanmeister$ java jar fcrepo-import-export-0.1.1.jar --mode export --resource http://localhost:8080/rest -dir /tmp/example_bag --binaries --bag-profile metaarchive --bag-config /tmp/bagit-config.yml

ERROR 09:47:30.573 (ImportExportDriver) Error performing import/export: The specified bag config file does not exist: /tmp/bagit-config.yml

 

Do I need to create the metaarchive bag config file? 

 

Thanks,

 

Sam

Yes, you need to create a 'bagit-config.yml' file as described here:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export#running-the-importexport-utility-with-a-bagit-support

Thanks Andrew. 

 

I created a config.yml file and then ran the utility again and successfully created a bag that meets the MetaArchive bagit profile expectations. 

Here is export bag-info.txt file: 

 

Samuels-Educopia-MacBook-Pro-8:example_bag samalanmeister$ cat bag-info.txt

Payload-Oxum : 1327.1

Bagging-Date : 2017-07-17

Bag-Size : 1 KB

Source-Organization : MetaArchive Member

Organization-Address : Member address

Bag-Group-Identifier : SAMPLE

External-Identifier : SAMPLE_001

Internal-Sender-Identifier : SAMPLE_001

Contact-Email : member@metaarchive.org

Contact-Phone : +14047832534

Internal-Sender-Description : Sample bag exported from fcrepo

External-Description : Sample bag exported from fcrepo

Contact-Name : Member Rep Name

Samuels-Educopia-MacBook-Pro-8:example_bag samalanmeister$

 

Anything else you need from me?

Thanks for doing this verification, Sam Meister.

It looks like the bagit-info.txt that you generated conforms to the profile in the code base:

  • https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/src/main/resources/profiles/metaarchive.json

 

I have created a follow-on ticket to actually enable the metaarchive.json profile within the code such that provided yml configuration files can be verified against the expected fields.

It would be very helpful if you could be available to run a similar test once the following ticket has been worked (which will likely not be in the very near term):
- https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2537

Andrew, 

 

Sounds good. Yes, I'd be happy to run another test when ready.

renderedFields.description:
This task is to verify the BagIt profile created in: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2223

Potentially useful instructions:

  1. Download the utility:
    https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/releases
  1. Have a running Fedora
    If you do not have a Fedora to test with, you may want to start up the "one-click run":
    https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FEDORA4x/Quick+Start#QuickStart-One-ClickRun
  1. Have data in your Fedora
    If you do not have data in your Fedora, you will likely want to load some of your own or one of the existing example datasets:
    https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-sample-dataset/tree/master/additional_datasets

Although there are minimal instructions in the readme linked above, if you run into issues loading any of these datasets, I would be happy to help... the possibility of issues arising is not inconceivable.

  1. Export your data as Bagit bags
    Here are some minimal instructions:
    https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/blob/master/README.md#running-the-importexport-utility-with-a-bagit-support

To export APTrust-style bags, use the ''--bag-profile aptrust" argument when running the utility.

The question to be answered is: Are the APTrust-style bags that the utility creates actually compliant with the APTrust expectations/requirements?
